properties.areaDesc: Northern Washington Coast; Grays Harbor County Coast
properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 8 at 5:32AM PST until November 8 at 10:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously large breaking waves along the coast.

* WHERE...Northern Washington Coast and Grays Harbor County
Coast zones.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM PST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous breaking waves can knock people off their
feet and sweep them into the ocean. Driftwood and debris in
powerful surf can injure or even kill people on the beach
observing the ocean. High surf will result in erosion to
beaches, dunes, and bluffs and may cause damage to roads,
trails, and coastal structures.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Caution should be used when in or near
the water, especially those who will be participating in razor
clam digging.
properties.instruction:
Everyone should remain out of the water and well back from the
surf zone. This includes staying off jetties, piers, and other
coastal structures. Never turn your back on the ocean and keep
children and pets close. Know the tides and forecast conditions.
Follow warning signs and respect barriers.

NWSheadline: HIGH SURF WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 10 PM PST THIS EVENING

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 8 at 7:28AM CST by NWS Brownsville TX
properties.description:
At 728 AM CST, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm over
Armstrong, moving northeast at 25 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 40 mph and half inch hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Armstrong, Kenedy County Wind Farms, U S 77 Border Patrol Station,
and Armstrong Ranch Airport.

This includes US Highway 77 between mile markers 722 and 740.
properties.instruction:
If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

Torrential rainfall is also occurring with this storm and may lead to
localized flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded
roadways.

This storm may intensify, so be certain to monitor local radio
stations and available television stations for additional information
and possible warnings from the National Weather Service.

NWSheadline: A STRONG THUNDERSTORM WILL IMPACT NORTHWESTERN KENEDY COUNTY THROUGH 800 AM CST

properties.areaDesc: Hidalgo, TX
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued November 8 at 7:19AM CST until November 8 at 9:15AM CST by NWS Brownsville TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southeastern Hidalgo County in deep south Texas...

* WHEN...Until 915 AM CST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 718 AM CST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 0.5 and 1.5 inches of rain
have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Weslaco, Alamo, Donna, Elsa, Progreso, Edcouch, La Villa, Maria
Alicia P Munoz Elementary School, Olivarez, Midway North, Donna
High School, Weslaco High School, Donna Police Department, Donna
City Hall, Donna Public Library, Midway South, Mila Doce, Sam
Houston Elementary School, Alameda Park and A.p. Solis Middle
School.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

NWSheadline: FLOOD ADVISORY IN EFFECT UNTIL 915 AM CST THIS MORNING

properties.description:

thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between 3
and 5 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to
2 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing
or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Benavides, Concepcion, Ramirez, Realitos, Rios and Cruz Calle.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.areaDesc: Central Coast of Oregon
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 8 at 3:58AM PST until November 8 at 10:00PM PST by NWS Portland OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Large waves and hazardous surf conditions. Breakers up to
33 feet on the beaches.

* WHERE...Central Coast of Oregon.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM PST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties,
and other structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off
rocks and jetties and drown while observing high surf. Minor
beach erosion may damage coastal properties and buildings.
Higher than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low-
lying shoreline.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Caution should be used when in or near the
water, especially those who will be razor clamming. Keep
children and pets away from the surf zone. Keep off of jetties,
rocks and logs near the surf zone. If you see someone swept into
the sea do not swim in after them. Call 911 and keep an eye on
them until help arrives.
properties.instruction:
A High Surf Advisory means that high surf will affect beaches,
producing rip currents, sneaker waves and beach erosion. Stay
well back from the water's edge and be alert for exceptionally
high waves.

Keep away from large logs on the beach. Water running up on the
beach can easily lift or roll logs which can injure or kill
someone caught in their path.

NWSheadline: HIGH SURF ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 10 PM PST THIS EVENING FOR BEACHES

properties.areaDesc: Northern Coastal Humboldt
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 8 at 3:24AM PST until November 8 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves 22 to
24 feet. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, High astronomical
tides will cause minor flooding in low lying areas around
Humboldt Bay. Up to one half foot of saltwater inundation
above ground level is possible near shorelines and tidal
waterways. Between 8.7 and 8.9 feet MLLW at the North Spit
tide gauge is predicted.

* WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, from 7 AM this morning to 10
PM PST this evening. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 10 AM
this morning to noon PST today. High tide is at 10:21 AM at the
Humboldt Bay North Spit tide gauge. Saltwater inundation will
be possible 1 to 2 hours before and after high tide.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low lying areas around Humboldt Bay
including parks and roads with only isolated closures
expected. Flooding will likely impact Jackson Ranch Road in
the Arcata Bottoms and several roads in King Salmon. Dangerous
surf conditions and localized beach erosion. Beachcombing is
highly discouraged!.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The large surf on Sunday will coincide
with high astronomical tides and high tidal anomalies. This
will allow significant runup onto area beaches and may impact
normally dry land or even roads or parking lots.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory indicates that onshore winds and tides
will combine to generate flooding of low areas along the shore.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.

Large breaking waves along the coast will lead to increased wave
run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.
Use extra caution near the surf zone as these large waves will be
capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 8 at 3:24AM PST until November 8 at 10:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Large breaking waves 22 to 24 feet.

* WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal
Mendocino Counties.

* WHEN...From 7 AM this morning to 10 PM PST this evening. .

* IMPACTS...Dangerous surf conditions and localized beach
erosion. Beachcombing is highly discouraged!.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The large surf on Sunday will coincide
with high astronomical tides and high tidal anomalies. This
will allow significant runup onto area beaches and may impact
normally dry land or even roads or parking lots.
properties.instruction:
Large breaking waves along the coast will lead to increased wave
run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.
Use extra caution near the surf zone as these large waves will be
capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

properties.areaDesc: Northern Coastal Humboldt
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 8 at 3:24AM PST until November 8 at 10:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves 22 to
24 feet. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, High astronomical
tides will cause minor flooding in low lying areas around
Humboldt Bay. Up to one half foot of saltwater inundation
above ground level is possible near shorelines and tidal
waterways. Between 8.7 and 8.9 feet MLLW at the North Spit
tide gauge is predicted.

* WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, from 7 AM this morning to 10
PM PST this evening. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 10 AM
this morning to noon PST today. High tide is at 10:21 AM at the
Humboldt Bay North Spit tide gauge. Saltwater inundation will
be possible 1 to 2 hours before and after high tide.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low lying areas around Humboldt Bay
including parks and roads with only isolated closures
expected. Flooding will likely impact Jackson Ranch Road in
the Arcata Bottoms and several roads in King Salmon. Dangerous
surf conditions and localized beach erosion. Beachcombing is
highly discouraged!.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The large surf on Sunday will coincide
with high astronomical tides and high tidal anomalies. This
will allow significant runup onto area beaches and may impact
normally dry land or even roads or parking lots.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory indicates that onshore winds and tides
will combine to generate flooding of low areas along the shore.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.

and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.

capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean

caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact

closures.

properties.areaDesc: Zapata; Jim Hogg; Brooks; Starr
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued November 8 at 5:24AM CST until November 9 at 9:00AM CST by NWS Brownsville TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of Deep South Texas, including the following
counties, Brooks, Jim Hogg, Starr and Zapata.

* WHEN...Through Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur
in poor drainage and urban areas. Storm drains and ditches may
become clogged with debris.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Potential for heavy rainfall, including two windows where
rainfall rates could reach 2 inches per hour for two hours both
late tonight and early Sunday morning, and again Sunday night
through mid morning Monday.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.headline: Frost Advisory issued November 8 at 5:09AM CST until November 8 at 9:00AM CST by NWS Tulsa OK
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Dense Fog Advisory, visibility one quarter mile or
less in dense fog, especially near bodies of water and in valley
areas. For the Frost Advisory, temperatures as low as 33 will
result in frost formation.

* WHERE...In Arkansas, Benton, Carroll, Madison, and Washington
Counties. In Oklahoma, Craig, Delaware, Mayes, and Ottawa Counties.

* WHEN...Until 9 AM CST this morning.

* IMPACTS...Frost could harm sensitive outdoor vegetation. Sensitive
outdoor plants may be killed if left uncovered. Visibilities are
expected to be reduced to less than one quarter mile by dense fog.
Rapidly changing visibility will create hazardous driving
conditions.
properties.instruction:
Cover outdoor plants or bring them indoors.

If driving, slow down, use your low beam headlights, and leave plenty
of distance ahead of you.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Heavy mixed precipitation possible. Total snow accumulations
between 3 and 7 inches for Whittier, Eastern Turnagain Arm,
Girdwood, and from Moose Pass to north of Seward. Total snow
accumulations between 5 and 10 inches of snow from Turnagain Pass
to Tern Lake, including the Hope Cutoff. Ice accumulations around a
light glaze possible from Turnagain Pass to Tern Lake and up to one
tenth of an inch from the Hope Cutoff to Hope. Easterly winds 55 to
70 mph possible for Eastern Turnagain Arm Tuesday morning.

* WHERE...East Turnagain Arm, and Western Prince William Sound.

* WHEN...From Monday morning through Tuesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. The hazardous conditions
could impact the Monday evening and Tuesday morning commutes. Very
strong winds could cause extensive damage to trees and power lines.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A strong and complex weather system is
expected to move over the Kenai Peninsula beginning Monday morning.
Light snow to become steady by late Monday afternoon with snow,
heavy at times, Monday night through early Tuesday morning. East
winds from Prince William Sound will move through Whittier and
across Eastern Turnagain Arm Monday morning quickly changing the
snow at lower elevations to rain. At higher elevations, the snow
may become a wintry mix of snow, sleet, and freezing rain before
changing to rain. Any rain may also lead to slush and ponding of
water on roads. The easterly winds through Whittier and Eastern
Turnagain Arm may peak around 60 and 70 mph before diminishing
Tuesday afternoon.

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 8 at 4:04AM AST until November 9 at 6:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...High Rip Current Risk, life-threatening rip currents.

* WHERE...North-facing beaches of Puerto Rico, including Culebra.

* WHEN...Through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Lingering northerly swells generated by
distant surface low over the central Atlantic will support
breaking waves of 5 to 8 feet and a high risk of life-
threatening rip currents along the northern exposed beaches of
Puerto Rico and Culebra.
properties.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

NWSheadline: HIGH RIP CURRENT RISK REMAINS IN EFFECT THROUGH MONDAY AFTERNOON

properties.areaDesc: Municipality of Skagway; Haines Borough and Klukwan
properties.headline: Winter Storm Watch issued November 7 at 10:46PM AKST until November 10 at 3:00AM AKST by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
A strong system is expected to move through the area Sunday night
into Monday. Temperatures below freezing combined with snow levels
below 1,000 ft are indicative of snowfall for upper elevations. Mid-
level southeasterly flow suggests potential for White Pass to be
sheltered from much of the precipitation, putting them on the lower
end of the range. A band of precipitation looks to set up across the
Fairweather and Chilkat mountain ranges, increasing the likelihood of
the Haines Highway seeing periods of heavy snowfall on Monday.

* WHAT...Heavy snow possible. Total snow accumulations of 6 to 12
inches possible.

* WHERE...Haines Borough and Klukwan and Municipality of Skagway.

* WHEN...From late Sunday night through late Monday night.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The upper elevations of the Haines Highway
near Haines Customs and the Klondike Highway near White Pass.
Higher amounts expected for the Haines Highway.
properties.instruction: Monitor the latest forecasts for updates on this situation.

properties.areaDesc: Kenedy Island; Willacy Island; Cameron Island
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 8 at 1:07AM CST until November 9 at 6:00PM CST by NWS Brownsville TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Statement, isolated minor coastal
flooding expected. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous
rip currents expected.

* WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island
Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Statement, from noon CST today
through late tonight. For the High Rip Current Risk, from noon
CST today through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Wave run-up may approach the dunes along narrow
beaches. Beach equipment, such as umbrellas and chairs, could
be moved by waves. Vehicles driving along narrow beaches may
experience higher water levels. Elevated water levels may also
occur across the Laguna Madre and South Bay, and along State
Highway 4 west of Boca Chica State Park. Rip currents can
sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Max inundation is expected near high tide at
452 PM this afternoon.
properties.instruction:
Do not drive through flooded roadways.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued November 8 at 12:34AM CST until November 9 at 12:00PM CST by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of south Texas, including the following areas,
Aransas Islands, Bee, Coastal Aransas, Coastal Kleberg, Coastal
Nueces, Coastal Refugio, Coastal San Patricio, Duval, Goliad,
Inland Kleberg, Inland Nueces, Inland Refugio, Inland San Patricio,
Jim Wells, Kleberg Islands, La Salle, Live Oak, McMullen, Nueces
Islands and Webb.

* WHEN...Through Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Widespread forecast rainfall amounts of 2-5 inches will be common
across South Texas. Isolated amounts of 7 to 9 inches remains a
possibility, especially in the vicinity of training and slow
moving storms. While soils will be able to absorb most of this
moisture, the higher rainfall rates, slow storm motion, and
training can quickly lead to localized, urban flooding and in
locations with poor drainage.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.areaDesc: Aransas Islands; Kleberg Islands; Nueces Islands; Calhoun Islands
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 8 at 12:27AM CST until November 9 at 3:00AM CST by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents
expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal
flooding expected.

* WHERE...Aransas Islands, Kleberg Islands, Nueces Islands and
Calhoun Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, from 6 AM CST this
morning through late tonight. For the Coastal Flood Advisory,
from noon today to 3 AM CST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Rip currents can sweep even
the most experienced swimmers away from shore into deeper
water. These rip currents can become life-threatening to
anyone entering the surf.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore; San Francisco Peninsula Coast; Northern Monterey Bay
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued November 7 at 8:09PM PST until November 9 at 10:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1.6 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, an increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip
currents with breaking waves of 12 to 16 ft expected.

* WHERE...Pacific Coast.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement through Monday evening.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, through noon PST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Waves can sweep across the shoreline without
warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tide gauge, high tide
is expected to be: 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 10:06 AM
Sunday 11/8, 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 10:35 AM
Monday 11/9, 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 11:04 AM
Tuesday 11/10. These predictions include up to 1.2 ft of surge
that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

and Brevard Counties.

* WHEN...Through late Monday night.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away

properties.instruction:
Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 7 at 10:25AM MST until November 8 at 11:00PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Maricopa County in south central Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 1100 PM MST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the Verde River between Fort McDowell and the
Salt River is occurring. Recreation on or near the Verde River will
be unsafe.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1025 AM MST, A streamflow gauge on the Verde River near the
Salt River confluence measured a flow near or in excess of 2000
cfs.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Fort McDowell and any recreational areas along the Verde River
downstream towards the confluence with the Salt River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Flooding is occurring. It is important to know where you are relative
to streams, rivers, or creeks. Campers and hikers should avoid
streams or creeks.

Raceway and Arlington.
